scenario: AITA for reducing my tip to compensate for a drink I didn’t order? (US) | So short story, at a restaurant today for lunch I got an entree and a glass of water (not fancy water mind you, just tap and it didn’t even have ice). My girlfriend got the same entree and a tea. When the cheque came we had been charged the same amount, $10 for the entree and $2 for a “beverage”. When I pointed this out to the waitress she said water was a beverage and I needed to pay for it. When it came time to tip time I did the math for what I would usually tip, $2.50 tip for my $10 entree and then subtracted the price of the $2 tap water. Basically I left a .50 cent tip. My girlfriend thinks it was an asshole move and I think I’m not paying $2 for lukewarm tap water. basically I brought my cheque total to the $12.50 it would have originally been without the water added.

Strengthened Resilience and Adaptability** - **Problem-Solving Skills:** Juggling multiple demands trains your brain to think on your feet, prioritize efficiently, and find creative solutions under pressure. This can translate into a more resourceful and flexible mindset in other areas of life. - **Emotional Resilience:** Parenting and household management often involve dealing with unexpected challenges (e.g., illnesses, last-minute changes, or emotional outbursts). Heightened Awareness and Presence** - **Mindfulness in the Moment:** Your role requires constant awareness of others’ needs, which can foster a deeper sense of presence and attentiveness—not just to your children but to the world around you. This might translate into greater patience, empathy, or even a heightened appreciation for small joys. - **Multitasking Mastery:** While often criticized, multitasking in this context can sharpen your ability to juggle priorities without losing sight of the bigger picture. You’re essentially training your brain to filter what’s urgent vs. important. ### **3. A Shift in Perspective on Time and Priorities** - **Gratitude for Small Wins:** When every day is a whirlwind of tasks, you learn to celebrate incremental progress (e.g., "We made it through the day without meltdowns!").
